title: Spatial Temporal Analysis of Fieldwise Flow in Microvasculature
protocol: Acclimatize 9–10 week-old male C57BL/6 mice for at least 4 days.
Fast the mice for 16 hours prior to studies.
Weigh the animal.
Sedate the animal with 5% isoflurane.
Place the sedated mouse on a heating pad to maintain body temperature.
Use an oxygen flow rate of 1–2 L/min.
Maintain sedation with 1-2% isoflurane.
Check reflexes by toe pinch.
Monitor temperature using a rectal thermometer.
Monitor heart rate and respiration visually.
Shave the area for jugular cannulation placement.
Shave the area below the rib cage for liver exposure.
Make a 1 cm left ventral incision 1–2 cm below the mouse’s jaw for jugular cannulation.
Clear away all fat and fascia surrounding the jugular vein.
Tie off the anterior end of the jugular using 06 suture string to prevent bleeding.
Make a tiny nick in the jugular vein.
Slide the cannula (30 G x ½ in, needle), needle holder and polyethylene tubing (0.011 x 0.024 inches² attached to a Luer stub adapter) into the jugular for about 1 cm.
Secure the cannula at the posterior end of the jugular using suture string.
Fill the cannula with 0.9% saline and deliver 70 kDa fluorescein dextran (to a dose of 30 mg/kg via injection of 0.1 mL of a 9 mg/mL solution in saline) through the jugular cannula.
Make a 4–6 cm incision across the torso, 1–2 cm below the middle of the rib cage to expose the liver for imaging.
Place a wet (soaked in 0.9% saline) gauze sponge below the left lateral liver lobe.
Tape on the periphery of the glass window of a 40 mm coverslip-bottomed dish and apply cyanoacrylate adhesive to the tape.
Press the glass plate to the liver using cotton-tipped applicators.
Minimize tissue motion for microscopy by pressing the gauze into the glue on the tape.
Move the animal to the microscope stage.
Add sterile 0.9% saline into the coverslip-bottomed dish to keep the liver moist throughout the imaging session.
Maintain temperature at 36–37 °C via heating pads mounted on the stage, a heating pad placed over the animal and an objective heater.
Use a Xenon arc lamp for illumination.
Select fluorescein-specific excitation filters between 480–500 nm and emission filters between 507–543 nm.
Choose a Plan Fluor 20x, N.A. 0.75 water immersion objective.
Set the exposure time to allow acquisition at 100 fps.
Adjust illumination level to visualize red blood cell shadows and vasculature topology without phototoxicity or photobleaching.
Collect images at a rate of 100 fps.
Set camera pixel resolution between ~0.65 and ~1.3 µm/pixel.
Set frame size between 512 x 512 and 1024 x 1024 pixels.
Set bit depth between 8 and 16 bits.
Use the highest possible resolution, frame size, and bit depth that still allows for 100 fps image collection.
Save time series files as TIF sequences or native camera/microscope format if FIJI can open them.
Image multiple areas over time.
Maintain the mouse on the microscope stage for up to 2 hours.
Euthanize the mouse after imaging is complete.
Open the movie file in FIJI using File > Open or File > Import > Image sequence.
Select a single image from stable images between respirations where the vascular network is clear.
Duplicate the selected single image and save it in a new folder without spaces in file or folder names.
Set up a new blank TrakEM2 project by selecting File > New > TrakEM2 (blank).
Select the new folder containing the duplicated single image as the project folder.
Right-click in the main work area and select Import > Import Image.
Navigate to the saved single image and select it for import.
Right-click in the main work area again and select Display > Autoresize canvas/Layer set.
Left-click in the main work window to fill the image in the work area.
In the TrakEM2 Template section, right-click on "• anything" and select Add new child > area list.
Drag "Template > anything" onto "Project Objects > project".
Drag "Template > anything > • area list" onto "Project Objects > project > anything".
Create a bar labeled area list in the main TrakEM2 window under the Z space tab.
Select the paintbrush tool in the main TrakEM2 window.
Press Shift and roll the mouse wheel to select an appropriate size for the paintbrush.
Paint the vascular network using the paintbrush tool.
Hold down Alt while using the paintbrush tool to erase.
Save the TrakEM2 setup by pressing Control + S keys frequently.
Right-click in the main TrakEM2 window and select Export > AreaLists as labels (tif).
In the popup window, select Scale 100% and Export All area list.
Close TrakEM2 windows and choose yes for Save project.
Open the image of AreaLists and adjust Brightness/Contrast by pressing the auto button in the B&C window.
Select Image > Lookup Tables > Invert LUT to invert the lookup table.
Save this image of black labels on white background and close the image.
Open the labels file in FIJI.
Select Plugins > Skeleton > Skeletonize.
Save the skeletonized image as a tif.
Use the skeleton.tif file as one of the input files needed for STAFF flow analysis.
When saving the file, do not use spaces in the filename.
Manually edit the skeleton file as needed using the paint tool.
Place a gap at locations where branches in the vasculature have not been captured because they go out of the image plane.
Open the movie file in FIJI using File > Open or File > Import > Image sequence.
Select a time period of the image sequence for flow analysis where tissue position has remained stable over time, except during respiration.
Duplicate the selected portion of the sequence by typing in the numbers of the beginning and end frames under Image > Duplicate.
Check image spatial and temporal calibration under Image > Properties and correct if necessary.
Save the image file as a TIF (or as an uncompressed AVI) without including spaces in the file name.
Open the plugins folder in the FIJI folder.
Copy STAFF.ijm into the Macros folder: Fiji\plugins\Macros\STAFF.ijm.
Copy STAFF_Dir.jar into the plugins folder: Fiji\plugins\STAFF_Dir.jar.
Open the macros folder in the FIJI folder.
Inside this macros folder, open the AutoRun folder.
Copy STAFF_Loader.ijm into the AutoRun folder: Fiji\macros\AutoRun\STAFF_Loader.ijm.
Start FIJI and verify macro installation.
Select Plugins > Macros to check for installed commands.
If necessary, select Plugins > Macros > Install, then open the Fiji\plugins\Macros folder and select STAFF.ijm.
Click OK to install missing macros.
Create a new project in FIJI.
Select Plugins > Macros > Open-Create Project and follow prompts to create or update a configuration file.
Navigate to and select the Project Directory, Input File Folder, and input files Movie.tif and Skeleton.tif from the Open-Create Project menu.
Edit auto-populated output file names if necessary.
Input values for shortest segment length (20 µm), max speed measured (2,000 µm/s) and max speed mapped (1,000 µm/s).
Type in the values for pixel size and frame rate for the image sequence from metadata or experimental notes.
Check the Flicker Correction box if images have periodic background intensity flicker.
Select parameters for best visualization of the data.
Select max speed mapped to include about 95% of the data so that the data is mapped across the full range of the color scale.
Analyze the skeleton by selecting Plugins > Macros > Analyze Skeleton.
Wait for segment IDs to appear on the skeleton.
Observe the segment list appearing in the ROI manager.
Confirm that an ROI Manager file for the skeleton is saved and click OK.
Verify that between respiration movements, the skeleton remains over where red blood cells pass through the capillary.
Display the labeled segments as an overlay on the movie by opening the movie file and dragging the ROI zip file onto it.
Play the movie with the segments overlaid.
Select time intervals using Plugins > Macros > Select Time Intervals.
Wait while the macro generates a kymograph from a single segment over the total time for the movie.
Use Control + + keys to increase the size of the kymograph if needed.
Draw a rectangle around each time interval with the rectangle selection tool.
Click the T key or the Add button in the ROI manager to record time interval selections.
Repeat the process for as many time intervals as desired, making selections sequentially from the top (or left) to bottom (or right) of the kymograph.
Click OK in the Make an ROI for each time interval window.
Click OK in the popup window to confirm saved intervals in the Project Folder.
Select Plugins > Macros > Analyze Flow from the menu.
Edit values if necessary and click OK in the Analyze Flow Parameters dialogue box.
Edit file names if necessary and click OK in the Output File Names dialogue box.
Click OK to begin analysis when prompted.
Wait for a dialog box indicating that Flow Analysis is complete.
Confirm that results files have been stored as .csv format spreadsheet files in the Project Folder.
Watch as a temporal sequence of spatial maps of flow velocities is generated with color indicating flow speed.
Scroll through the .tif stack to visualize spatial and temporal variation in flow.
Save the stack as an AVI file (uncompressed for maximum portability) to share as a movie.
Open the segment_velocities.csv file in a spreadsheet or statistical analysis program.
Create a new spreadsheet page containing the absolute values of all velocity values from the segment_velocities.csv file.
Calculate overall average flow velocity using the absolute velocity values.
Determine average flow velocity for all vascular segments over time.
Calculate flow velocity for each vascular segment over time.
Generate histograms of velocity distributions.
Identify specific relevant segments in the labeled skeleton for regions of interest.
Perform analyses on selected segments to calculate values around specific morphological regions.
